sections.title: Two leaves for a lifetime
sections.text: This slow-growing desert gymnosperm is native to arid southwestern Angola and northwestern Namibia. It usually stands under 1 m tall, though exceptional plants may reach about 2 m, and its two persistent strap-shaped leaves can grow to several metres (up to about 4 m in published accounts). Continued growth at their bases and weathering make mature leaves split into ragged strips. The plate depicts the characteristic low trunk, paired long leaves and cones.

sections.title: Cones and longevity
sections.text: Welwitschia is dioecious: male and female cones are borne on separate plants, emerging near the leaf bases. Individual plants can live for many centuries, with some estimates exceeding 1,000 years. No food use is established by the cited botanical sources, so the leaves and cones are not described as edible.
